findings.text: follow-on: the comment introducing REQUEST_WAIT_SECONDS names a specific project (imas-ambix) and a dated incident, which reckon's repo-agnostic principle forbids in source and which reads as changelog prose. State the mechanism instead -- requests are rare and the loop's whole life is the read, so a child that exits while the FIFO is idle stays defunct -- with no project name or date.

follow-on: the change introduces load-bearing pending-buffer line reassembly in serve() (fleet_supervisor.py:1353-1362, splitting the read on newline and keeping the remainder), because os.read can return a partial line where the previous blocking readline could not. No case sends a request split across two writes, so a regression that dropped the pending buffer and dispatched an incomplete line would not be caught; add a case that writes a request in two fragments.

justifications.durability: The new case asserts observable behaviour, not implementation: it starts a short-lived child under the live serving loop, shows the reader's own pid present under /proc as a positive control, then requires the child's pid to leave /proc within COLLECT_SECONDS = 5.0 with no further request. I reproduced the declared mutation and the case reddens on it. Two residual gaps keep this below 20: the pending-buffer line reassembly the change introduces (fleet_supervisor.py:1353-1362) is load-bearing but no case sends a request split across reads to pin it, and readable_within's error path (returns False on OSError/ValueError) is not exercised. The wider-frequency waitpid(-1) sweep does not race a held Popen: the only waited child, _run_session_copy, is synchronous within the loop thread, and DeclaredServices._alive already falls back to its lock when another reaper has collected a service child.
justifications.evidence: The reviewed manifest records head 5db90a224 with a gate log; I re-ran the head arm myself in the reviewed worktree (the test process resolved the module to .../fleet-supervisor-collects-every-child/reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py): 19 passed, EXIT=0. I independently reproduced the declared negative control in a scratch extraction (base implementation b8cc7f0f plus the head test file): the named case test_an_exited_child_is_collected_with_no_request_arriving fails, 1 failed EXIT=1, an id the head arm passes, so the case discriminates and the guarded thing is made to happen. Held at 18, not 20, because the reviewed manifest declares baseline_suite and after_suite both null and names no base gate log, so the reviewed run's own added-failure delta is unmeasured.
justifications.fit: Names describe mechanism (readable_within, REQUEST_WAIT_SECONDS, REQUEST_READ_BYTES, COLLECT_SECONDS and the new case name) with no version, plan or ticket identifier and no attribution, and the updated docstrings state the rule. Held at 17 because a new source comment (fleet_supervisor.py:96) names a specific project (imas-ambix) and a dated incident, which reckon's repo-agnostic principle forbids in source and which reads as changelog prose rather than mechanism.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Plan section 4 asks that the supervisor collect exited children on a bounded interval while never racing the synchronous session-start wait. Both done-when items are delivered and I reproduced them: the request loop now waits on the FIFO with a bounded select (REQUEST_WAIT_SECONDS = 0.5, fleet_supervisor.py:1351) and calls _reap_finished_children (fleet_supervisor.py:1350) on each interval, so collection no longer depends on a request arriving. Section 4's hazard is met: the suite's autouse fixture isolated_config_home pins the services config inside each case's temporary tree, and no case starts a declared service.
justifications.reuse: The change reuses the existing _reap_finished_children and handle_line and adds one small helper, readable_within, over select rather than a bespoke read loop; the request path keeps one parser and one dispatch. No duplicated logic is introduced, and the previous os.fdopen wrapper is replaced by an explicit descriptor close in the existing finally.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat b8cc7f0f..5db90a224 lists exactly three changed paths: reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py, tests/test_fleet_supervisor.py and the evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/the-fleet-moves-to-a-new-node/fleet-supervisor-collects-every-child.html. All three are inside the manifest's declared write paths; the declared figures directory was not created because the done-when names no artifact. No shared index, sprint state, other plan or out-of-scope path is touched.
